# dsh-skill-groups
Quick-switch named **skill groups** for DSH. Some skills are situational: you want them the moment y
ou are doing research or trading, and you do not want them adding noise to the model's catalog the r
est of the time. This plugin groups skills and switches between the groups in one click.
## What it actually changes
Only **which skills the model can discover**. A masked skill:

- disappears from the session skill catalog (saving context on every step),
- is still invocable by

you with `/skill-name`,
- **is not deleted, moved, or rewritten on disk**, and
- keeps its real inst
ructions — the plugin holds the captured body from the discovered provider, so a masked skill never
degrades into a stub.
That last point is the reason the plugin does not rename files or edit `SKILL.md` frontmatter the wa
y some skill managers do: those approaches pollute git and desynchronise every `SKILL.md` on every s
skill managers do: those approaches pollute git and desynchronise every `SKILL.md` on every switch.
## Two kinds of group
| Kind | Behaviour |

| **Exclusive** | The "mode". Applying one automatically deactivates the other exclusive groups. |
|
**Additive** | Overlays. Any number can be on at once, for the handful of skills you always want. |
A skill in no group is governed by the *default policy* — visible by default, so installing this plu
gin can never silently take skills away.
## Where to switch
- **Composer chip** (`conversation.input.left`) — the group name sits beside the input box; click to

switch.
- **`/skillset <group>`** — from the composer. Also `/skillset off`, `/skillset add <group>

`, `/skillset rm <group>`.
- **`/skillset`** with no argument lists every group and its current stat

e.
- **Sidebar panel** — the full manager: groups, members, cost preview, auto rules, import/export,

undo.
- **Model tools** — `skillgroup_current`, `skillgroup_list`, `skillgroup_apply`, `skillgroup_
toggle`, `skillgroup_create`, `skillgroup_set_members`, `skillgroup_clear`, so you can just say "swi
tch me to research mode".
## Per-session, not global
A switch scopes to the session you made it in. Two conversations can run different groups at once, a
nd a new session falls back to your default. This is implemented with an agent-scoped skill provider
rather than a global one, so the isolation is real rather than cosmetic.
## Cost preview
Before switching you can see roughly what the group costs: the catalog characters and estimated toke
ns it puts in front of the model. Descriptions are counted at the host's own 500-character cap, so t
he number matches what the model actually receives.
## Auto-activation rules
Optional, off by default. A rule can activate a group by workspace path, agent preset, or keywords.
Rules only ever **activate** — an explicit switch always wins, and rules never deactivate something
ever **activate** — an explicit switch always wins, and rules never deactivate something you chose.
## Configuration
Installed through the plugin manager. Two switches: the sidebar entry and the composer chip. State l
ives in `$DSH_HOME/skill-groups/state.json` (atomic write; a corrupt file degrades to defaults rathe
E/skill-groups/state.json` (atomic write; a corrupt file degrades to defaults rather than throwing).
## Known limits

- Skills the host does not expose to `ctx.skills` cannot be grouped.
- MCP servers do **not** follow
a group. The host has no runtime MCP toggle, so coupling them would require a restart — out of scop

e rather than faked.
- `/skillset --for-turn` depends on a turn counter; if it cannot be resolved th
e switch is made persistent and says so.
